The 2020–21 season was [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]'s 29th season in the [[Premier League]] and their 46th consecutive season in the top flight of [[Football in England|English football]]. The club finished second in the [[2020–21 Premier League|Premier League]], their joint-highest finish since the retirement of [[Alex Ferguson]] in 2013, were knocked out of the [[2020–21 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] in the semi-finals by [[Manchester derby|local rivals]] [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], in the quarter-finals of the [[2020–21 FA Cup|FA Cup]] by [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] and finished third in their [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] group, therefore being relegated to the [[2020–21 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League]].

The season threatened to be overshadowed by the attempted formation of a [[European Super League]]. On 18 April 2021, Manchester United announced they were joining 11 other European clubs as founding members of the Super League, a proposed 20-team competition intended to rival the [[UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/leading-football-clubs-announce-new-super-league-competition-18-april-2021|title=Leading football clubs announce new Super League competition}}</ref> The announcement drew an unprecedented backlash from supporters, other clubs, media partners, sponsors, players and the [[Government of the United Kingdom|UK Government]], forcing the club to withdraw just two days later.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thebusbybabe.sbnation.com/2021/4/20/22394177/manchester-united-figures-react-to-super-league-news|title=Manchester United figures react to Super League news|date=20 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/man-united-super-league-sponsors-20431669|title=Brands halted sponsorship talks with Premier League clubs over Super League|date=21 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-56822592|title=European Super League offends principles of competition - Boris Johnson|work=BBC News|date=20 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european-super-league-keir-starmer-b1834111.html|title=Keir Starmer urges government to block English clubs' involvement in European Super League|website=[[Independent.co.uk]]|date=20 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/official-statement-on-man-utd-withdrawal-from-european-super-league|title=Manchester United to withdraw from European Super League}}</ref> The failure of the project led to the resignation of executive vice-chairman [[Ed Woodward]], while [[2021 Old Trafford protests|resultant protests]] against Woodward and owners [[Glazer ownership of Manchester United|the Glazer family]] led to a [[pitch invasion]] ahead of a league match against Liverpool on 2 May 2021, which saw a Premier League game get postponed due to supporter protests for the first time in the competition's history.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/manchester-united/story/4365318/woodward-out-as-manchester-united-executive-vice-chairman|title=Woodward resigns as Man United vice-chairman|date=20 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56960091|title=Man Utd v Liverpool off after protest|work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On the pitch, United equalled the biggest win in Premier League history with a [[Manchester United F.C. 9–0 Southampton F.C.|9–0]] victory against [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] on 2 February 2021,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55806211|title=Man Utd beat nine-man Southampton 9-0|work=BBC Sport}}</ref> but ended the season with defeat on penalties in the [[2021 UEFA Europa League final|UEFA Europa League final]] against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]], going four straight seasons without a trophy and one season away from equalling their worst trophy drought since the club was [[1973–74 Manchester United F.C. season|last relegated]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/solskjaer-shown-up-familiar-failings-extend-man-utd-trophy/tam5tdvdhrln17nc9z7vw7vwt |title=Solskjaer shown up as familiar failings extend Man Utd's trophy drought {{pipe}} Goal.com |access-date=29 June 2021 |archive-date=28 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210628190009/https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/solskjaer-shown-up-familiar-failings-extend-man-utd-trophy/tam5tdvdhrln17nc9z7vw7vwt |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/manchester-united/tab/honours/|title=Manchester United football club honours}}</ref>

==Pre-season and friendlies==
Due to the belated end to the [[2019–20 Manchester United F.C. season|previous season]] as a result of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|COVID-19 pandemic]], Manchester United played just one friendly before the start of their 2020–21 Premier League season, away to [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] on 12 September 2020.<ref>{{cite news |first=Adam |last=Marshall |title=Villa game is perfect for United's preparation |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-villa-friendly-perfect-chance-to-prepare-for-new-season |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=10 September 2020 |access-date=10 September 2020 }}</ref> Aston Villa's [[Ollie Watkins]] scored the only goal of the game in the 16th minute.<ref>{{cite news |first=Samy |last=Kadiri |title=Friendly: Aston Villa 1 United 0 |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/aston-villa-v-man-utd-friendly-match-report-12-september |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=12 September 2020 |access-date=14 September 2020 }}</ref>

==Premier League==
Manchester United's opening match of the [[2020–21 Premier League]] season was due to be away to [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] on 12 September, but was postponed to ensure a minimum of 30 days between seasons, as per Premier League regulations; the club's final game of the [[2019–20 Manchester United F.C. season|2019–20 season]] was on 16 August.<ref>{{cite news |first=Samuel |last=Luckhurst |title=Manchester United get Premier League fixtures boost |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/man-united-fixture-news-burnley-18798540 |work=Manchester Evening News |publisher=MEN Media |date=20 August 2020 |access-date=10 September 2020 }}</ref> Instead, United began their season on 19 September at home to [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]]. After [[Andros Townsend]] opened the scoring for the visitors early on, [[David de Gea]] denied [[Jordan Ayew]] from the penalty spot in the second half, only for the video assistant referee (VAR) to intervene as De Gea had advanced from his line before Ayew had struck the ball; former Manchester United winger [[Wilfried Zaha]] scored from the re-take. [[Donny van de Beek]], making his debut after coming on midway through the second half, pulled a goal back for United, but Zaha scored a third for Palace five minutes later, making him the first former United player to score more than one Premier League goal in a single match against United. It was the third time United had lost their opening home match of a Premier League season and the first since [[2014–15 Manchester United F.C. season|2014–15]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 1-3 Crystal Palace: Wilfried Zaha scores twice against former club |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54127842 |work=BBC Sport |date=19 September 2020 |access-date=20 September 2020 }}</ref> The following week, away to [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]], United came back from a goal down via an own goal by [[Lewis Dunk]] and one from [[Marcus Rashford]] – the 10,000th goal in the club's history<ref>{{cite news |first=Joe |last=Ganley |title=Milestone for Marcus as he hits our 10,000th goal |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/manchester-united-hit-10000-goals-in-all-competitions-with-rashford-strike |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=26 September 2020 |access-date=6 October 2020 }}</ref> – to lead 2–1 as the match entered stoppage time at the end of the second half; however, as additional time drew to an end, [[Solly March]] equalised for the home side. As United searched for a last-minute winning goal, the referee blew the final whistle with the score at 2–2, only for the VAR to award a penalty to United for a handball by [[Neal Maupay]]. [[Bruno Fernandes]] scored the penalty to give United their first league win of the season.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=Dawkes |title=Brighton 2-3 Man Utd: Dramatic injury-time penalty gives Manchester United victory |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54215333 |work=BBC Sport |date=26 September 2020 |access-date=30 September 2020 }}</ref>

In the following match on 4 October, the last before the international break, a Bruno Fernandes penalty gave United an early lead at home to [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], who were led by former United manager [[José Mourinho]]; however, Spurs overturned the deficit thanks to [[Tanguy Ndombele]] and [[Son Heung-min]]. After United [[Forward (association football)|forward]] [[Anthony Martial]] was sent off for slapping [[Erik Lamela]] in the face, [[Harry Kane]] scored a brace, Son added a second goal and [[Serge Aurier]] also scored to give Tottenham a 6–1 win. It was Manchester United's joint-biggest defeat in the Premier League, matching the scoreline from the [[Manchester derby]] in 2011, as well as the heaviest defeat under either [[Ole Gunnar Solskjær]] as manager or [[Ed Woodward]] as executive vice-chairman. The four goals United conceded in the first half was the most they had conceded at home in a single half since November 1957, also against Tottenham.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Man Utd 1-6 Tottenham: Son Heung-min, Harry Kane score |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54313274 |work=BBC Sport |date=4 October 2020 |access-date=4 October 2020 }}</ref> United returned from the international break with a trip to [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] on 17 October, and went behind early on to a [[Luke Shaw]] own goal. After [[Harry Maguire]] equalised with a header midway through the first half, Fernandes had a penalty saved by Newcastle goalkeeper [[Karl Darlow]] in the second, the first he had failed to score since joining the club in February. He eventually scored in the 86th minute, followed by goals from [[Aaron Wan-Bissaka]] in the 90th – the first of his senior career – and Rashford in the sixth minute of added time.<ref>{{cite news |first=Saj |last=Chowdhury |title=Newcastle 1-4 Man Utd: Visitors produce late flourish to earn welcome win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54489181 |work=BBC Sport |date=17 October 2020 |access-date=17 October 2020 }}</ref> On 24 October, United were held to a goalless draw by Chelsea.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 0-0 Chelsea: Hosts still searching for first home win this season |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54580512 |work=BBC Sport |date=24 October 2020 |access-date=24 October 2020 }}</ref> The result meant the club had failed to win any of their first three home league games for the first time since [[1972–73 Manchester United F.C. season|1972–73]]; however, the result also extended United's unbeaten league record against Chelsea to six matches, with the most recent defeat coming in November 2017, while Chelsea had not won a league match at Old Trafford since the [[2012–13 Manchester United F.C. season|2012–13 season]].

On 1 November, United played [[Arsenal F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|rival]] [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] at home. [[Paul Pogba]]'s foul inside the box led to [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang]]'s winning penalty as Arsenal won a league match at Old Trafford for the first time since 17 September 2006.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 0-1 Arsenal: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang penalty decides tight encounter |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54679344|work=BBC Sport |date=1 November 2020 |access-date=6 November 2020 }}</ref> Before the international break, United travelled to [[Everton F.C.|Everton]]. The visitors won 3–1; Fernandes scored his first brace of the season before [[Edinson Cavani]] sealed the victory deep into the added time with his first United goal.<ref>{{cite news |first=Alistair |last=Magowan|title=Everton 1-3 Manchester United: Bruno Fernandes scores twice at Goodison |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54758065|work=BBC Sport |date=7 November 2020 |access-date=7 November 2020 }}</ref> Two weeks later, United returned to action at home against [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]]. A retaken penalty from Fernandes – given after Albion's goalkeeper, former United shot stopper [[Sam Johnstone]] stepped out of the line before saving the first – secured United's maiden home league win of the season.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 1-0 West Bromwich Albion: Bruno Fernandes penalty earns win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54941199|work=BBC Sport |date=21 November 2020 |access-date=21 November 2020 }}</ref> On 29 November, United visited [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]]. Trailed 2–0 at half-time by goals from [[Jan Bednarek (footballer)|Jan Bednarek]] and [[James Ward-Prowse]], United came back to win 3–2 via Fernandes and a brace from Cavani. Goalkeeper [[Dean Henderson]] made his league debut for the club, coming on at the interval for the injured De Gea. The win made United the first side in Premier League history to win four consecutive away games despite trailing in everyone of them, and also made United won eight consecutive top-flight away matches for the first time in their history.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Southampton 2-3 Man Utd: Sub Edinson Cavani inspires comeback win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55032760|work=BBC Sport |date=29 November 2020 |access-date=30 November 2020 }}</ref>

On 5 December, United played [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] at the [[London Stadium]]. Henderson, on his first league start for the club, conceded to [[Tomáš Souček]] in the first half. In the second half, the visitors produced yet another comeback to win 3–1; Pogba and [[Mason Greenwood]] scored their first league goals of the season, before Rashford sealed the club's ninth straight away victory in the league.<ref>{{cite news|title=West Ham United 1-3 Manchester United: Visitors come from behind again|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55111845|first=Harry|last=Poole|work=BBC Sport|date=5 December 2020|access-date=5 December 2020}}</ref> The next week, United were held 0–0 at home by [[Manchester derby|derby rivals]] [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]; this was the first derby played at Old Trafford to end goalless since October 2015, and it was United's third consecutive clean sheet against City in all competitions, the longest since a run of four – all in the league – between 1994 and 1995.<ref>{{cite news|title=Manchester United 0-0 Manchester City: Derby ends in stalemate at Old Trafford|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55197158|work=BBC Sport|date=12 December 2020|access-date=12 December 2020|first=Phil|last=McNulty}}</ref> On 17 December, United managed yet another away comeback in a 3–2 win at [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]], extending the club record to 10 consecutive league away wins. Rashford's two goals and Martial's first league goal of the season were enough to cancel out [[David McGoldrick]]'s brace and keep Sheffield United winless after their first 13 league games of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Sheffield United 2-3 Manchester United: Marcus Rashford scores twice for visitors|first=Alistair|last=Magowan |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55255038|work=BBC Sport|date=17 December 2020|access-date=17 December 2020}}</ref> On 20 December, United went rampant as they beat their [[Leeds United F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|"Roses" rival]] [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] 6–2 at home. Meeting for the first time in the league since 2004, McTominay opened the game with a brace inside three minutes, becoming the first player to do so in the league's history. Fernandes scored in the 20th minute before [[Victor Lindelöf]] scored his first goal of the season to put United 4–0 up after just 37 minutes. [[Liam Cooper]] pulled one back for the visitors before half time. [[Daniel James (footballer)|Daniel James]] scored his first league goal of the season midway through the second half, before Fernandes scored a penalty in the 70th minute. Three minutes later, [[Stuart Dallas]] scored Leeds' second to close the match. This was the first league match in which United scored more than five goals since the [[Manchester United F.C. 8–2 Arsenal F.C.|8–2 win over Arsenal]] in August 2011.<ref>{{cite news |first=Matthew |last=Howarth|title=Manchester United 6-2 Leeds United: Hosts up to third after thumping win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55291044 |work=BBC Sport |date=20 December 2020 |access-date=20 December 2020 }}</ref> United opened the Boxing Day matchday with a visit to [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]]. Leading twice via Rashford and Fernandes with [[Harvey Barnes]]' goal sandwiched in between, United substitute defender [[Axel Tuanzebe]] scored an own goal after diverting [[Jamie Vardy]]'s attempt to make the score 2–2.<ref>{{cite news |first=Mantej |last=Mann|title=Leicester City 2-2 Manchester United: Foxes earn a late point |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55373753|work=BBC Sport |date=26 December 2020 |access-date=26 December 2020 }}</ref> The club ended 2020 with a home game against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]]. Rashford scored at 92:51 – United's latest winning goal at Old Trafford in the Premier League since [[Michael Owen]] on 20 September 2009 (95:27) – to make United end the year in second place.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 1-0 Wolverhampton Wanderers: Too early for title talk, says Marcus Rashford |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55406822|work=BBC Sport |date=29 December 2020 |access-date=29 December 2020 }}</ref>

On New Year's Day, United hosted [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] in the second game of the matchweek. Martial scored first after 40 minutes before [[Bertrand Traoré]] equalises in the 58th minute. Fernandes sealed the win via a penalty three minutes later after referee [[Michael Oliver (referee)|Michael Oliver]] judged that Pogba had been fouled by [[Douglas Luiz]] inside the box.<ref>{{cite news|title=Manchester United 2-1 Aston Villa: Bruno Fernandes penalty puts Red Devils joint top|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55444188|first=Michael|last=Beardmore|work=BBC Sport|date=1 January 2021|access-date=2 January 2021}}</ref> On 12 January, United visited [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] for the game in hand from the first matchday. Pogba volleyed in the only goal of the game to send United top of the table with a three-point lead over defending champions and [[Liverpool F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|arch rivals]] [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], whom they would meet in the following match.<ref>{{cite news|title=Burnley 0-1 Manchester United: Paul Pogba winner sends Red Devils top of Premier League|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54038551|first=Simon|last=Stone|work=BBC Sport|date=12 January 2021|access-date=13 January 2021}}</ref> Both teams would only fire blanks as the said match ended goalless, keeping United top while Liverpool were down to fourth below Manchester City and Leicester City upon both sides' win in this matchday.<ref>{{cite news|title=Liverpool 0-0 Man Utd: Alisson saves thwart leaders at Anfield|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55607090|work=BBC Sport |first=Phil|last=McNulty|date=17 January 2021|access-date=17 January 2021}}</ref> Three days later, they played [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] away. [[Ademola Lookman]] scored after five minutes to give Fulham the early lead. Cavani equalised 16 minutes later after a mistake by Fulham goalkeeper [[Alphonse Areola]]. United completed another comeback in the 65th minute by Pogba's long-range curling effort, sending United back to the top of the table after starting the match in third.<ref>{{cite news|title=Fulham 1-2 Man Utd: Paul Pogba fires United back to the top of the Premier League|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55642375|first=Phil|last=Dawkes|work=BBC Sport|date=20 January 2021|access-date=20 January 2021}}</ref> On 27 January, United played the first return leg of the league season as they hosted bottom-placed Sheffield United. The visitors' [[Kean Bryan]] opened the scoring after 23 minutes to end the first half 1–0 up. Maguire equalised in 64th minute only to be cancelled by [[Oliver Burke]] as Manchester United were defeated in the league for the first time in 14 matches while Sheffield United earned only their second win of the league season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Man Utd 1-2 Sheff Utd: Oliver Burke scores winner for Blades|first=Shamoon|last=Hafez |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55728232|work=BBC Sport|date=27 January 2021|access-date=27 January 2021}}</ref> United ended January with a visit to [[Arsenal F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|rivals]] Arsenal. The match ended goalless as the visitors, still searching for a first league win in this fixture since April 2018, including all five league meetings under Solskjær, managed to deny [[Mikel Arteta]] from becoming the first Arsenal manager to win his first three matches against United.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Arsenal 0-0 Manchester United: Alexandre Lacazette hits bar for Gunners |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55769177 |work=BBC Sport |date=30 January 2021 |access-date=30 January 2021 }}</ref>

United began February with a [[Manchester United F.C. 9–0 Southampton F.C.|9–0]] victory over Southampton that equalled their own record for the [[Premier League records and statistics#Scorelines|biggest home win in the Premier League]], set in [[Manchester United F.C. 9–0 Ipswich Town F.C.|1995]], while the visitors equalled their worst Premier League defeat, set in [[Southampton F.C. 0–9 Leicester City F.C.|2019]]. Eight different players scored, including an own goal by [[Jan Bednarek (footballer)|Jan Bednarek]] and the record-equalling goal scored by James. Martial, who came on at half-time, was the only player to score more than once.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Man United 9-0 Southampton: United score nine against Saints |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55806211 |work=BBC Sport |date=2 February 2021 |access-date=2 February 2021 }}</ref> Four days later, United twice lost the lead in a 3–3 draw against Everton. Cavani and Fernandes scored past Everton's second-choice keeper [[Robin Olsen]] in the first half, only for [[Abdoulaye Doucouré]] and [[James Rodríguez]] to level the scores three minutes apart from each other. McTominay restored the lead only for [[Dominic Calvert-Lewin]] to equalise again in the final minute of stoppage time following Tuanzebe's foul on Everton substitute and fellow United Academy graduate [[Joshua King (footballer, born 1992)|Joshua King]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 3-3 Everton: Dominic Calvert-Lewin scores late goal to deny hosts |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55867139 |work=BBC Sport |date=6 February 2021 |access-date=6 February 2021 }}</ref> On Valentine's Day, United visited West Bromwich Albion. Albion's loanee forward [[Mbaye Diagne (footballer)|Mbaye Diagne]] rubbed Lindelöf's face off upon scoring inside 83 seconds. Fernandes equalised with a volley in the 44th minute following a cross from Shaw. In the second half, Maguire had a penalty cancelled by referee [[Craig Pawson]] after a stumble with [[Semi Ajayi]] was judged by VAR [[Jonathan Moss (referee)|Jonathan Moss]] as not a foul.<ref>{{cite news |first=Shamoon|last=Hafez |title=West Brom 1-1 Man Utd: Bruno Fernandes scores stunning volley |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55967799|work=BBC Sport |date=14 February 2021 |access-date=14 February 2021 }}</ref> Facing Newcastle United the next Sunday, Rashford opened the scoring before [[Allan Saint-Maximin]] made the equaliser six minutes later. In the second half, Fernandes assisted James' goal and scored a penalty himself to secure a 3–1 win. Forward [[Shola Shoretire]] made his first team debut as he came on for Rashford.<ref>{{cite news |last=Magowan|first=Alistair|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56033730 |title=Manchester United 3-1 Newcastle United: Marcus Rashford plays key role in home win |work=BBC Sport|date=21 February 2021|access-date=21 February 2021}}</ref> United ended the month with a 28 February visit to Chelsea. A presumed handball from [[Callum Hudson-Odoi]] resulted in a penalty cancelled by the VAR as the fixture ended goalless again, extending United's unbeaten league record against Chelsea to seven matches.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil|last=McNulty|title=Premier League: Chelsea 0-0 Man Utd – More VAR controversy in stalemate|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56143444|work=BBC Sport|date=28 February 2021|access-date=28 February 2021}}</ref>

March began with a visit to Selhurst Park, where United had not been beaten in the previous 11 fixtures and won the last four. The former record was extended but not so for the latter; United failed to get revenge on Crystal Palace for their home defeat in September, as the match ended in a 0–0 draw.<ref>{{cite news |first=Gary|last=Rose|title=Crystal Palace 0-0 Manchester United: Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's side held in dull encounter |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56178109|work=BBC Sport|date=3 March 2021|access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref> On 7 March, United visited [[Manchester derby|derby rivals]]' home and in-form league leaders Manchester City. Fernandes scored a penalty in the second minute after [[Gabriel Jesus]]' foul on Martial in the box. Shaw scored United's second goal five minutes into the second half – his first league goal since August 2018 – as United won for the third successive time at the [[City of Manchester Stadium]] and tighten the gap to 11 points; this was City's first defeat in 20 league matches, breaking their 21-match winning run across all competitions.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil|last=McNulty|title=Man City 0-2 Man Utd: Bruno Fernandes & Luke Shaw seal derby win|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56227458|work=BBC Sport|date=7 March 2021|access-date=7 March 2021}}</ref> The next week, United hosted West Ham. An own goal by [[Craig Dawson]] following a shot from McTominay was the only goal scored as the hosts returned to the second place.<ref>{{cite news|first=Simon|last=Stone|title=Manchester United 1-0 West Ham: Own goal separates sides|work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56247548|date=14 March 2021|access-date=14 March 2021}}</ref>

Following the international break at the end of March, United returned to action with a home game against Brighton. Despite starting brightly, it was the visitors who took the lead through former United striker [[Danny Welbeck]] in the 13th minute. Rashford levelled the scores just after the hour mark, before Greenwood sealed the win with a header seven minutes from the end, the eighth time in 2020–21 that they have won after being in a losing position. It was only the second time in the Premier League that United had come from behind to do the double over an opponent in a single season; the other being was against Southampton in [[2012–13 Manchester United F.C. season|2012–13]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 2-1 Brighton & Hove Albion: Mason Greenwood scores winner |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56553200 |website=BBC Sport |date=4 April 2021 |access-date=4 April 2021 }}</ref> On 11 April, United travelled to London to play Tottenham. Cavani seemingly scored an opener for the visiting side, but the goal was ruled out after it was seen by VAR that McTominay had hit [[Son Heung-min]] in the face and the goal was ruled out. Just moments later, Son scored the actual opener and gave the home side the lead. Twelve minutes into the second half, Fred scored his first league goal for United since September 2018 to equalise the score. Cavani then scored for real in the 79th minute, giving United the lead. In the final minute of stoppage time, Greenwood scored to secure a win for United and extended their unbeaten away run in the league to 23 matches.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil|last=McNulty|title=Tottenham Hotspur 1-3 Man Utd: Edinson Cavani scores as visitors fight back|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56629082|work=BBC Sport|date=11 April 2021|access-date=11 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Harry|last=Robinson|title=United have the chance to match historical record in 2020/21 |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/unbeaten-run-extended-to-23-games|website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=11 April 2021|access-date=11 April 2021}}</ref> In the next game against Burnley, Greenwood scored two goals which sandwiched [[James Tarkowski]]'s equaliser before Cavani sealed the 3–1 win in the added time.<ref>{{cite news |first=Alex|last=Bysouth|title=Manchester United 3-1 Burnley: Mason Greenwood scores twice for hosts |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56706888|work=BBC Sport|date=18 April 2021|access-date=18 April 2021}}</ref> The final league match of April saw Manchester United's first visit to [[Leeds United F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|"Roses" rival]] Leeds' [[Elland Road]] since October 2003, which ended goalless.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon|last=Stone |title=Leeds United 0-0 Manchester United: Red Devils held to Elland Road stalemate |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56790342 |work=BBC Sport|date=25 April 2021|access-date=25 April 2021}}</ref>

The 2 May match against [[Liverpool F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|rivals]] Liverpool was postponed due to [[Glazer ownership of Manchester United#European Super League|anti-Glazer protests]] at Old Trafford.<ref name="MUNLIVprotests">{{cite news |title=Manchester United v Liverpool game postponed after fan protest |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56960091 |work=BBC Sport |date=2 May 2021 |access-date=2 May 2021 }}</ref> The match at Aston Villa on 9 May saw United trailed by Traoré's first half goal. In the second half, Fernandes scored a penalty kick following Douglas Luiz's foul on Pogba, before Greenwood and Cavani completed their 10th Premier League comeback of the season, the most for any club in a single season.<ref>{{cite news |first=Harry|last=Poole|title=Aston Villa 1-3 Man Utd: Red Devils' comeback keeps Man City waiting on title |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56960426|work=BBC Sport|date=9 May 2021|access-date=9 May 2021}}</ref> Two days later, United hosted Leicester by fielding a much-changed starting line-up. Left-back [[Luke Thomas (footballer, born 2001)|Luke Thomas]] opened the scoring after 10 minutes, this was his first goal for Leicester's first team. Greenwood equalised five minutes later, but Leicester got their winning goal via a thumping header from center-back [[Çağlar Söyüncü]], his first goal since November 2019 as local rivals Manchester City were confirmed Premier League champions for the fifth time, all within the past 10 years. This was United's first league defeat since another 1–2 against Sheffield United in January 2021.<ref>{{cite news|first=Simon|last=Stone|title=Man City Premier League champions as Leicester City beat Manchester United|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56990159 |work=BBC Sport|date=11 May 2021|access-date=11 May 2021}}</ref> This was also United's first home defeat to Leicester since 31 January 1998, and the first successive defeat to Leicester in all competitions since 1973.<ref>{{cite web |title=Manchester United football club: record v Leicester City|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/manchester-united/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Leicester%20City/ |website=11v11.com |access-date=11 May 2021}}</ref> Two days later, United finally hosted Liverpool. Fernandes opened the scoring after 10 minutes and lasted 24 minutes before [[Diogo Jota]]'s equaliser. [[Roberto Firmino]] scored twice to bring the visitors 3–1 up. Rashford pulled one back but [[Mohamed Salah]] sealed the game to send Liverpool to fifth. This was United's first home league defeat to Liverpool since the 0–3 in March 2014, with Firmino the first Liverpool player to score a league brace at Old Trafford since [[Steven Gerrard]], who did it in the aforementioned match.<ref>{{cite news|first=Simon|last=Stone|title=Manchester United 2-4 Liverpool: Visitors boost top-four hopes with win|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56876294|work=BBC Sport|date=13 May 2021|access-date=13 May 2021}}</ref> On the final home match of the season, United played the already-relegated Fulham. Cavani's shot from 40 yards opened the scoring chart, but [[Joe Bryan]] equalised later on.<ref>{{cite news|first=Simon|last=Stone|title=Manchester United 1-1 Fulham: Edinson Cavani scores stunner in Man Utd draw |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57066741|work=BBC Sport|date=18 May 2021|access-date=18 May 2021}}</ref> Leicester's defeat to Chelsea later that night secured United's second place finish.<ref>{{cite news|first=Emlyn|last=Begley|title=Chelsea 2-1 Leicester City: Blues beat Foxes in crucial top-four showdown|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57066729|work=BBC Sport|date=18 May 2021|access-date=18 May 2021}}</ref> On the final matchday on 23 May, in the away match against Wolverhampton, [[Anthony Elanga]] headed home his first senior goal before equaliser by [[Nélson Semedo]]. [[Romain Saïss]]' foul on Van de Beek inside the box resulted in a penalty for United executed by [[Juan Mata]], who slotted the ball in to secure a 2–1 win in Wolves' manager [[Nuno Espírito Santo]]'s final match in charge of the club. United thus became only the fourth side to remain unbeaten away from home in an entire English top-flight campaign, stretching from the first season in [[1888–89 Football League|1888–89]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Gary|last=Rose |title=Wolves 1-2 Manchester United: Nuno Espirito Santo beaten in final game |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57132113|work=BBC Sport|date=23 May 2021|access-date=23 May 2021}}</ref>

==FA Cup==
As a Premier League side, Manchester United entered the [[2020–21 FA Cup]] in the Third Round Proper along with the other Premier League and Championship clubs. For this round, they were drawn at home against Championship side [[Watford F.C.|Watford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2020/nov/30/emirates-fa-cup-third-round-proper-draw-301120 |title=Premier League and Championship clubs join Emirates FA Cup after third round draw|publisher=The Football Association|date=30 November 2020|access-date=30 November 2020}}</ref> United took the lead via stand-in captain [[Scott McTominay]] inside five minutes, it was the only goal of the game as the hosts won 1–0.<ref>{{cite news |last=Stone |first=Simon |title=Man Utd 1-0 Watford: Scott McTominay heads early FA Cup winner at Old Trafford |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55574516 |access-date=9 January 2021 |work=BBC Sport |date=9 January 2021}}</ref> The draw for the fourth and fifth round were made on 11 January, conducted by [[Peter Crouch]].<ref>{{cite web |title=The Emirates FA Cup fourth and fifth round draw made |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2021/jan/11/emirates-fa-cup-fourth-and-fifth-round-draws-20211101 |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=11 January 2021|date=11 January 2021}}</ref> They were drawn against [[Liverpool F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|arch rivals]] [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]].<ref>{{cite news |title=FA Cup draw: Manchester United to host Liverpool in fourth round |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55622538|access-date=11 January 2021 |work=BBC Sport |date=11 January 2021}}</ref> Liverpool took the lead through [[Mohamed Salah]] after 18 minutes, before [[Mason Greenwood]]'s equaliser eight minutes later. [[Marcus Rashford]] scored the second, only to be equalised by Salah. Substitute [[Bruno Fernandes]] then scored the match-deciding free kick 12 minutes from time as United won 3–2, earning their first victory against Liverpool in all competitions since March 2018.<ref>{{cite news |last=Stone |first=Simon |title=Manchester United 3-2 Liverpool: Bruno Fernandes settles FA Cup thriller |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55708043|access-date=24 January 2021 |work=BBC Sport |date=24 January 2021}}</ref> In the fifth round, they played host to [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]]. McTominay scored seven minutes into extra time to send the home side into the quarter-finals for the seventh successive season, equalling the club's longest home winning run in the competition (nine), set between 1908 and 1912. The match was also the first in English football to have a concussion substitute, as West Ham's [[Issa Diop (footballer)|Issa Diop]] did not return for the second 45 minute-half following his collision with [[Anthony Martial]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Stone |first=Simon |title=Manchester United 1-0 West Ham: Ole Gunnar Solskjaer praises 'low' players for bouncing back |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55951207 |access-date=9 February 2021 |work=BBC Sport |date=9 February 2021}}</ref> In the quarter-finals, United were defeated 3–1 by [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]], the club's first domestic away loss since January 2020. [[Kelechi Iheanacho]] struck first before being equalised by Greenwood. In the second half, goals from [[Youri Tielemans]] and Iheanacho sealed Leicester's first FA Cup semis in [[1981–82 FA Cup|39 years]] and the first win against United in any competition since the 5–3 win in the league in September 2014.<ref>{{cite news |last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Leicester City 3-1 Man Utd: Foxes into FA Cup semi-finals |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56415040|access-date=21 March 2021 |work=BBC Sport |date=21 March 2021}}</ref>

==EFL Cup==
Manchester United received a bye to the third round of the [[2020–21 EFL Cup]], having finished third in the [[2019–20 Premier League]] and thus qualified for the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League]]. The draw took place on 6 September 2020 and paired United with the winners of the second round tie between [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] and [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]], both of the [[EFL Championship|Championship]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Carabao Cup third round: Man City-Bournemouth, Lincoln-Liverpool, Luton-Man Utd |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54169912 |work=BBC Sport |date=16 September 2020 |access-date=22 September 2020 }}</ref> Luton won that match 1–0 and hosted the third round match on 22 September.<ref>{{cite news |title=Reading 0-1 Luton Town: Jordan Clark goal sets up Man Utd Carabao Cup tie |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54067073 |work=BBC Sport |date=15 September 2020 |access-date=22 September 2020 }}</ref> United took the lead just before half-time through a [[Juan Mata]] [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty kick]]. In the second half, goalkeeper [[Dean Henderson]], making his first-team debut, denied Luton an equaliser with a one-handed save from [[Tom Lockyer (footballer)|Tom Lockyer]], before substitutes [[Marcus Rashford]] and [[Mason Greenwood]] both scored in the last couple of minutes to give United a 3–0 win.<ref>{{cite news |title=Luton 0-3 Manchester United: Dean Henderson thrilled with "unbelievable" debut |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54190604 |work=BBC Sport |date=22 September 2020 |access-date=22 September 2020 }}</ref>

In the fourth round, the club was drawn against the winners of the match between [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] and [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Carabao Cup fourth-round draw completed before third-round games played |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54199445 |work=BBC Sport |date=17 September 2020 |access-date=22 September 2020 }}</ref> which Brighton won 2–0.<ref>{{cite news |title=Preston North End 0-2 Brighton & Hove Albion: Seagulls set up Man Utd tie |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54190605 |work=BBC Sport |date=23 September 2020 |access-date=24 September 2020 }}</ref> The match came just four days after the two sides had met in the league, and saw [[Scott McTominay]] and [[Paul Pogba]] score their first goals of the season, while Juan Mata was again on the scoresheet to give United a 3–0 win.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=Dawkes |title=Brighton 0-3 Man Utd: Paul Pogba strikes as United reach Carabao Cup quarters |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54298218 |work=BBC Sport |date=30 September 2020 |access-date=30 September 2020 }}</ref>

In the quarter-finals, United were again given an away draw, this time against fellow Premier League club [[Everton F.C.|Everton]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Carabao Cup quarter-final draw: Holders Manchester City face Arsenal |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54380549 |work=BBC Sport |date=1 October 2020 |access-date=2 October 2020 }}</ref> Playing before 2,000 spectators, United won 2–0 via late goals from [[Edinson Cavani]] and [[Anthony Martial]].<ref name="LC-QF">{{cite news |title=Everton 0-2 Manchester United: Edinson Cavani stunner helps visitors into Carabao Cup semi-finals |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55327849 |work=BBC Sport |date=23 December 2020|first=Alistair |last=Magowan |access-date=23 December 2020 }}</ref>

In the semi-finals, they met [[Manchester derby|derby rivals]] [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] at home. The clubs had met thrice in this round – in [[1969–70 Football League Cup|1969–70]], [[2009–10 Football League Cup|2009–10]], and [[2019–20 EFL Cup|2019–20]]; the team progressed from each of these ties would gone on to win the trophy. City, the EFL Cup holders for three consecutive seasons, progressed to the record-equalling fourth final in a row with a 2–0 victory over a defensively poor United, who suffered a fourth consecutive cup competition semi-final exit.<ref>{{cite news |title=Man Utd 0-2 Man City: Pep Guardiola's side reach Carabao Cup final|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55481278|work=BBC Sport |first=Simon|last=Stone|date=6 January 2021 |access-date=6 January 2021}}</ref>

==UEFA Champions League==
===Group stage===
{{main|2020–21 UEFA Champions League group stage}}
United qualified for the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League]] after finishing third in the [[2019–20 Premier League]]. This was their 23rd UEFA Champions League campaign, more than any English club. The draw for the group stage took place in [[Geneva]], Switzerland on 1 October 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=UEFA Champions League group stage draw |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/draws/2021/2001252/ |website=UEFA.com |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=1 October 2020 |access-date=1 October 2020 }}</ref> The club was drawn in Group H with [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]], [[RB Leipzig]] and Champions League group stage debutants [[İstanbul Başakşehir F.K.|İstanbul Başakşehir]]. This was United's first meeting with Paris Saint-Germain since the [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Paris Saint-Germain v Manchester United|2018–19 round of 16 tie]], which United won on away goals through a stoppage time penalty, while they had never met Leipzig and Başakşehir.

In the first group match, United got a 2–1 away win at Paris Saint-Germain; goals from [[Bruno Fernandes]] and [[Marcus Rashford]] cancelled out [[Anthony Martial]]'s own goal.<ref>{{cite news |first=Tom |last=Rostance |title=Paris St-Germain 1-2 Man Utd: Marcus Rashford hits late winner|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54559717 |work=BBC Sport |date=20 October 2020 |access-date=20 October 2020 }}</ref> United then beat [[RB Leipzig]] 5–0 in the second match a week later; [[Mason Greenwood]] opened the scoring in the first half, Rashford scored his first senior hat-trick after coming on as a second-half substitute, and Martial also scored a late penalty. Rashford's hat-trick was the first scored by a United substitute since current manager Solskjær did so against [[Nottingham Forest F.C. 1–8 Manchester United F.C.|Nottingham Forest in 1999]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Shamoon |last=Hafez |title=Man Utd 5-0 RB Leipzig: Mason Greenwood, Marcus Rashford hat-trick, Anthony Martial score |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54710550 |work=BBC Sport |date=28 October 2020 |access-date=28 October 2020 }}</ref> It was United's eighth hat-trick in the Champions League, scored by six different players. It was the club's first in the competition since [[Wayne Rooney]] against Club Brugge in the [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League qualifying phase and play-off round#Club Brugge v Manchester United|2015–16 play-off round]], their first in the Champions League proper since [[Robin van Persie]] against Olympiacos in the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Manchester United v Olympiacos|2013–14 knockout phase]], and the first in the competition's group stage since [[Michael Owen]] against Wolfsburg in the [[2009–10 UEFA Champions League group stage#Wolfsburg v Manchester United|2009–10 season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Three is the Magic Number!|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/collection/detail/collection-of-man-utd-champions-league-hat-tricks |publisher=Manchester United |date=30 October 2020 |access-date=31 October 2020 }}</ref> Spanning 16 minutes, it was also the quickest of the five [[List of UEFA Champions League hat-tricks|hat-tricks]] scored by substitutes in the competition's history.{{citation needed|date=March 2021}}

In the third match, United lost 2–1 away to İstanbul Başakşehir, who had former United defender [[Rafael (footballer, born 1990)|Rafael]] in their team. Former Chelsea forward [[Demba Ba]] gave Başakşehir their first ever goal in the Champions League on the way to claiming their first point – and first win – in the competition. The result ended United's club record 10-match winning streak on the road in all competitions, stretching back to a 1–1 draw with Tottenham in June 2020; it was also their first away defeat in all competitions in 19 matches, stretching back to January 2020.<ref>{{cite news |first=Shamoon |last=Hafez |title=Istanbul Basaksehir 2-1 Man Utd: Demba Ba, Edin Visca, Anthony Martial score |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54799454|work=BBC Sport |date=4 November 2020 |access-date=4 November 2020 }}</ref>

In the return leg 20 days later, United got their revenge against Başakşehir by winning 4–1. Fernandes scored twice inside 20 minutes before Rashford slotted home a penalty to bring United led by three goals at half-time in a Champions League game for the first time since the [[2006–07 UEFA Champions League knockout stage#Manchester United v Roma|7–1 win over Roma in April 2007]]. A direct free-kick goal from [[Deniz Türüç]] – the first to be scored in the Champions League against United since [[Franck Ribéry]] in [[2009–10 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Bayern Munich v Manchester United|March 2010]] – was cancelled out by [[Daniel James (footballer)|Daniel James]], who scored at home for the first time since August 2019.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon|last=Stone |title=Man Utd 4-1 Istanbul Basaksehir: Bruno Fernandes gives up hat-trick chance to keep his word |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54559717 |work=BBC Sport |date=24 November 2020 |access-date=25 November 2020}}</ref>

On 2 December, United were defeated 3–1 by Paris Saint-Germain, with a brace from [[Neymar]] and a goal from [[Marquinhos]] cancelled Rashford's, who scored for the third consecutive match against the Parisians.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon|last=Stone |title=Manchester United 1-3 Paris St-Germain: Neymar scores twice for Parisians|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55135808 |work=BBC Sport |date=2 December 2020 |access-date=2 December 2020}}</ref> The next week, Leipzig also got their revenge by winning 3–2 with goals from [[Angeliño]], [[Amadou Haidara]], and [[Justin Kluivert]]; Angeliño's goal at 1:49 was the quickest Champions League goal scored against United since [[Alan (footballer, born 1979)|Alan]]'s for Sporting Braga in [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League group stage#Manchester United v Braga|October 2012]] (1:27). United scored two late goals via Fernandes and [[Ibrahima Konaté]]'s own goal but their Champions League time was up before they could get the equaliser needed to progress. This was the first time since both legs of the [[2002–03 UEFA Champions League knockout stage#Quarter-finals|quarter-final in 2002–03]] that they conceded three or more goals in consecutive Champions League games while Solskjær became the first manager of an English club to lose at least six times in his first 10 Champions League games, having lost in 2018–19 against Paris Saint-Germain at home [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Manchester United v Paris Saint-Germain|in the round of 16]] and both of the season's [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Quarter-finals|quarter-final matches]] versus [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=Dawkes|title=RB Leipzig 3-2 Man Utd: Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's side knocked out of Champions League|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55219522 |work=BBC Sport |date=8 December 2020 |access-date=8 December 2020}}</ref>

==UEFA Europa League==
===Knockout phase===
{{main|2020–21 UEFA Europa League knockout phase}}
As one of the third-place finishers in the Champions League group stage, United entered the [[2020–21 UEFA Europa League knockout phase|UEFA Europa League knockout phase]]. This was their fifth Europa League campaign, having also entered in the knockout phase in [[2011–12 UEFA Europa League|2011–12]] and [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League|2015–16]] as well as starting at the group stage during their [[2016–17 UEFA Europa League|2016–17 winning campaign]] and [[2019–20 UEFA Europa League|2019–20]].

In the round of 32, United were drawn against Spanish club [[Real Sociedad]], whom they last met in the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League group stage#Real Sociedad v Manchester United|2013–14 UEFA Champions League group stage]].<ref>{{cite news |title=UEFA Europa League round of 32 draw |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/draws/2021/2001241/ |website=UEFA.com |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=14 December 2020 |access-date=18 December 2020 }}</ref> The first leg was played at [[Juventus Stadium]] in Turin due to travel restrictions relating to the COVID-19 pandemic. Former United winger [[Adnan Januzaj]], playing against the club for the first time since he was sold to Sociedad in July 2017, had the first chance of the tie, but United went on to win 4–0 with two goals from [[Bruno Fernandes]] and one each from [[Marcus Rashford]] and [[Daniel James (footballer)|Daniel James]]. Winger [[Amad Diallo]] made his first-team debut for the club when he came on for [[Mason Greenwood]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Rostance |first=Tom |title=Real Sociedad 0-4 Manchester United: Bruno Fernandes scores double in emphatic win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56103400|access-date=18 February 2021 |work=BBC Sport |date=18 February 2021}}</ref> In the return leg at Old Trafford, [[Mikel Oyarzabal]]'s missed penalty and a goal from [[Axel Tuanzebe]] that was disallowed for a foul by Lindelöf meant the match finished as a goalless draw. Forward [[Shola Shoretire]] made his European debut when he came on for Greenwood and became the youngest United player to appear in a European fixture, beating the record of [[Norman Whiteside]] by 108 days.<ref>{{cite news |last=Stone |first=Simon |title=Manchester United 0-0 Real Sociedad (Agg 4-0): Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's side advance in Europa League |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56185909|access-date=25 February 2021 |work=BBC Sport |date=25 February 2021}}</ref>

In the round of 16, United were drawn against Italian club and fellow former UEFA Champions League winner [[A.C. Milan|Milan]], whom they last met in the [[2009–10 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Manchester United v Milan|2009–10 UEFA Champions League knockout phase]].<ref>{{cite news |title=UEFA Europa League round of 16 draw |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/draws/2021/2001242/ |website=UEFA.com |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=26 February 2021 |access-date=26 February 2021 }}</ref> This would be their first meeting outside the European Cup/UEFA Champions League.<ref>{{cite web |title=Manchester United football club: record v AC Milan|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/manchester-united/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/AC%20Milan/|website=11v11.com |access-date=28 February 2021}}</ref> In the first leg, Amad scored first – his maiden goal for United – only to be equalised by [[Simon Kjær]] in the stoppage time.<ref>{{cite news|last=Stone|first=Simon|title=Manchester United 1-1 AC Milan: AC Milan late equaliser denies United|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56351824|access-date=11 March 2021|work=BBC Sport|date=11 March 2021}}</ref> In the second leg, substitute [[Paul Pogba]], playing his first game since 6 February 2021, scored the only goal as United progressed to the quarter-finals with a 2–1 aggregate win. Former United striker [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]] played against the club for the first time since leaving for [[LA Galaxy]] in March 2018 and nearly equalised via a header saved by goalkeeper [[Dean Henderson]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Sutcliffe|first=Steve|title=AC Milan 0-1 Man Utd (1-2 agg): Paul Pogba scores winner as visitors into Europa League last eight|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56433793|access-date=18 March 2021|work=BBC Sport|date=18 March 2021}}</ref>

In the quarter-finals, United were drawn against another Spanish club in the form of [[Granada CF|Granada]], whom they never played against before.<ref name="QF_SF_draws">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/draws/2021/2001243/ |title=UEFA Europa League quarter-final and semi-final draws |website=UEFA.com |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=19 March 2021 |access-date=19 March 2021}}</ref> This was the first season in their history that United faced more than one Spanish opposition. United won the first leg 2–0 with goals scored by Rashford and Fernandes, the club's first ever consecutive European away win against Spanish sides. Rashford became the first Englishman to score eight European competition proper goals in a single season since [[Bobby Charlton]] in [[1964–65 Manchester United F.C. season|1964–65 season]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Emons|first=Michael|title=Granada 0-2 Manchester United: Marcus Rashford and Bruno Fernandes on target in first leg|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56667352|access-date=8 April 2021|work=BBC Sport|date=8 April 2021}}</ref> In the return leg, a goal from [[Edinson Cavani]] and an own goal from [[Jesús Vallejo]] ensured United's passage to the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 2-0 Granada (agg 4-0): Reds set up Europa League semi-final against Roma |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56713064 |work=BBC Sport |date=15 April 2021 |access-date=15 April 2021 }}</ref>

In the semi-finals, United met Italian club [[A.S. Roma|Roma]], whom they last met in the [[2007–08 UEFA Champions League knockout stage#Manchester United v Roma|2007–08 UEFA Champions League knockout stage]]. After scoring first via Fernandes, United fell behind to goals from [[Lorenzo Pellegrini]]'s penalty and former Manchester City forward [[Edin Džeko]]. In the second half, United scored five without reply; Fernandes scored his second via a penalty, Cavani scored a brace, with Pogba and Greenwood scoring one each to secure a first-leg win of 6–2. This made United the first side to score six goals in a major European competition's semi-final since [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] won [[1963–64 European Cup#Semi-finals|6–0]] against [[FC Zürich|Zürich]] in 1964.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 6-2 Roma: United win eight-goal thriller in Europa League semi-final |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56892065 |work=BBC Sport |date=29 April 2021 |access-date=29 April 2021 }}</ref> The second leg was a tight one; United scored first through Cavani only to be reversed by Džeko and [[Bryan Cristante]]. Cavani scored again, but [[Nicola Zalewski]]'s goal, which later would reassigned as [[Alex Telles]]' own goal, sent Roma to their first victory over United since [[2006–07 UEFA Champions League knockout stage#Roma v Manchester United|2007]]. However, United still went through with an 8–5 aggregate win as manager Solskjær progressed to his first final as United's manager, the club's first European final since the victorious [[2017 UEFA Europa League final]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Roma 3-2 Man Utd (5-8 on aggregate): Solskjaer's side through to Europa League final |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57000593|work=BBC Sport |date=6 May 2021 |access-date=6 May 2021 }}</ref>

In the final, they met first-time finalists [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]], United's third Spanish opposition this season. The clubs previously met four times, in the [[2005–06 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group D|2005–06]] and [[2008–09 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group E|2008–09]] Champions League group stages. All ended in goalless draws.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/teams/te2102/villarreal-cf/records-all-time-appearances/ |title=Villarreal CF » Record against Manchester United |website=WorldFootball.net |access-date=6 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Manchester United football club: record v Villarreal |url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/manchester-united/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Villarreal/ |website=11v11.com |access-date=6 May 2021}}</ref> The final was held on 26 May 2021, on the 22nd anniversary of the now-manager [[Ole Gunnar Solskjær]]'s winning goal in the [[1999 UEFA Champions League final|UEFA Champions League final]] and also would have been the 112th birthday of former manager [[Matt Busby]], who won the club its first European title in [[1968 European Cup final|1968]]. This match ended in a 1–1 draw after 120 minutes; [[Gerard Moreno (footballer)|Gerard Moreno]] stroke first before Cavani equalised in 55th minute. [[David de Gea]] became the last kicker in the penalties and the only one failed to score, as his was saved by [[Gerónimo Rulli]], handing Villarreal their first ever major trophy and their head coach [[Unai Emery]], formerly of Arsenal, his record fourth UEFA Cup/Europa League title, surpassing three-time winner [[Giovanni Trapattoni]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Villarreal 1-1 Manchester United (11-10 on pens): David de Gea spot kick saved in epic Europa League final shootout |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57224112|work=BBC Sport |date=26 May 2021 |access-date=26 May 2021 }}</ref> Some of the team were later criticised on social media for removing their silver medal on field, or even refused to wear one.<ref>{{cite news |first=Rob |last=Swan|title=Man United players criticised for reaction to Europa League runners-up medals |url=https://www.givemesport.com/1698046-man-united-players-criticised-for-reaction-to-europa-league-runnersup-medals|work=Give Me Sport |date=27 May 2021 |access-date=29 May 2021 }}</ref>
